The series is trend_dominated and the leader uses inverse error weighting. Given the high predictability, I will test if a more concentrated softmax_neg_error weighting performs better.
Testing if selecting the best model at each horizon step improves performance, given the moderate ranking stability.

The series is trend_dominated, and the current leader is a weighted combination. I will test if the DBA (Dynamic Baseline Averaging) combination method can capture the strong trend more effectively than the current weighted error approach.
The series has moderate ranking stability and a few high-error models; I will test if a trimmed mean on the full pool is more robust than the current weighted leader.
Testing if the median is more robust to the high error spread than the current weighted leaders.

The current leader is the median of the full pool, likely because the high error spread (relative spread 46.57) allows outlier models to degrade weighted averages. I will test if applying a weighted combination (as suggested by the diagnosis) to a more concentrated pool of the top 7 models (pool5) can outperform the median.

The series is trend_dominated (trend strength 0.9668), and the current leader is the median of the full pool. This suggests that high-error models are distorting the mean; I will test whether a mean of only the top 7 models can outperform the median of the entire pool by effectively excluding those outliers.
Given the moderate ranking stability, I want to test if a per-horizon approach can better capture the changing model performance across the forecast steps.

Since the series is trend_dominated and the current leader is a simple mean of a high-performing subset (pool6), I want to test if a weighted combination using softmax_neg_error on a slightly different subset (pool4) can improve the score.

The moderate ranking stability (tau 0.407) suggests that model performance might fluctuate across the horizon, so I will test a per-horizon top-k weighting strategy using the previously prepared handle w8.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.1215. Series context: trend strength 0.9668 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.407); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 46.569.
